newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moulinex stock down on capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex stock down on capital increase.

text.p: Shares in French appliance manufacturer Moulinex fell on Monday after the company announced a capital increase of 525 million francs at 93 francs per share.
But analysts said the terms of the capital increase were not unfavourable and they said the share selling was not too surprising given the stock's strong recent gains.

"When the news comes out, even if it's expected, there's some pulling out," a trader said. Shares in Moulinex, which announced the terms on Friday, were down 2.33 percent at 126 francs at 1140 GMT after recovering from an early low of 122.10.
The CAC 40 index was 0.2 percent higher.
The share has gained 6.9 percent since January after a strong rise in the second half of 1996 following the announcement last June of a drastic restructuring plan.

"The share is down because some people are anticipating dilution in the future. At 93 francs, it's a bit dilutive compared with the 110 franc or 115 franc price expected by some," said an analyst. But she added that she did not believe the fall in the share price was justified.
Another analyst said the dilution would be negligible. He said the use of the capital to pay down debt and the resulting drop in financial expense would be very positive for Moulinex.
Moulinex announced the broad lines of the capital increase in December and said at the time that it expected its biggest shareholders to subscribe.
On Friday it said they would subscribe for a total of 40 percent of the issue -- a fact viewed favourably in the market.
In a prospectus published on Monday that it expected its 1996/97 operating profit to exceed the 54 million francs of the previous year.
